newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Union Texas in Pakistan oil search near India border.
newsitem.headline: Union Texas in Pakistan oil search near India border.

text.p: Union Texas Pakistan Inc said on Monday it would start deep drilling of an exploratory oil and gas well in eastern Sindh province, about 65 km (40 miles) from the Indian border, early next year.
"Union Texas will start drilling in early 1997 near the Indian border," Charles Latch, president of the company in Pakistan, told reporters.

The company had completed 572 km of seismic data acquisition since it was granted the Eastern Sindh Concession in April 1994, Latch said. "Interpretation of all data (is) in hand with the first deep well test scheduled for early 1997."
Latch said Union Texas was likely to spend about $50 million on exploration and $40 million on operations in Pakistan in 1997, but the figures were not final.
The company had drilled 101 exploratory wells in Pakistan by April 1996 since it started work in 1977. It had made 44 discoveries and abandoned 57 as dry wells, he said.
"We are aggressively seeking new exploration opportunities," Latch said. "Union Texas has made 38 percent of all discoveries in Pakistan."

"A record production of over 30,000 barrels of oil per day and over 200 million cubic feet per day of gas has been achieved by Union Texas Pakistan (in 1996)," Latch said. "This is a significant increase over that of January 1, 1996 which was 20,585 barrels of oil and 176 million cubic feet of gas daily."
Union Texas accounts for about 40 percent of Pakistan's crude oil output and nine percent of its natural gas production.
"Our mission is to be the leader in Pakistan's energy sector through superior performance, growth in our core business and expansion into other energy-related opportunities," he said.
The company plans to lay oil and gas pipelines and set up an oil refinery. "The plans are in initial stages," he said.

Pakistan's total recoverable reserves are estimated at 400 million barrels of oil and 29 trillion cubic feet of proven associated and non-associated gas. Of these totals, about 275 million barrels of oil and eight trillion cubic feet of gas have already been produced, one analyst said.
